title: A Choice Before the Result
fact_notes: 人物・出来事・制度は架空の教材例。実在の調査・統計・実証結果ではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: Imagine two students choosing which of two unfamiliar competitions to enter during their school holiday.
sentences.ja: 休暇中に未知の二つの大会のどちらに参加するか選ぶ生徒二人を想像しよう。

sentences.en: Both examine the available information, compare the requirements, and discuss the likely demands on their time.
sentences.ja: 双方が情報を調べ条件を比較し時間的負担の見込みを話し合う。

sentences.en: They eventually make different choices because their interests and previous experiences lead them to value different opportunities.
sentences.ja: 関心や経験により異なる機会を重視するため別々の選択をする。

sentences.en: At this point, neither student knows whether the event selected will turn out as expected.
sentences.ja: この時点では選んだ行事が予想通りになるか誰も知らない。

sentences.en: After the holiday, one student returns with a prize while the other describes an event that was unexpectedly disorganized.
sentences.ja: 休暇後一人は賞を得て戻りもう一人は予想外に運営が混乱した行事を語る。

sentences.en: Their classmates immediately describe the first student's decision as sensible and the second student's decision as a mistake.
sentences.ja: 級友はすぐ第一の判断を賢明と、第二を誤りと評する。

sentences.en: Their teacher asks whether the judgments would have been different if the two outcomes had been reversed through circumstances beyond the students' control.
sentences.ja: 教師は本人の制御を超える事情で結果が逆になっていたら判断も違ったか尋ねる。

sentences.en: The question encourages the class to distinguish the quality of a decision from the quality of its eventual outcome.
sentences.ja: 問いは判断の質と最終結果の質を区別するよう促す。

sentences.en: The students review the information that had been available before each decision was made, rather than treating later discoveries as though they had been known beforehand.
sentences.ja: 後から分かったことを事前に既知だったかのように扱わず決定前に利用できた情報を見直す。

sentences.en: They notice that the student who encountered difficulties had actually investigated the competition more thoroughly than his successful classmate.
sentences.ja: 困難に遭遇した生徒は成功した級友より徹底的に大会を調べていたと気づく。

sentences.en: Conversely, the student who received a prize acknowledges that a favorable change in the competition's schedule had helped her perform well.
sentences.ja: 逆に受賞した生徒は大会の日程の好都合な変更が好成績に役立ったと認める。

sentences.en: The outcome alone therefore provides an incomplete basis for evaluating their earlier reasoning.
sentences.ja: したがって結果だけでは以前の推論を評価する不完全な根拠しか得られない。

sentences.en: This distinction does not mean that people should disregard the results of their decisions.
sentences.ja: この区別は判断の結果を無視すべきという意味ではない。

sentences.en: Unexpected consequences may reveal weaknesses in assumptions or identify information that would be useful in a future situation.
sentences.ja: 予期せぬ結果は前提の弱点や将来有用な情報を示し得る。

sentences.en: However, learning from an outcome requires examining why it occurred instead of simply attaching praise or blame to the person who made the decision.
sentences.ja: しかし結果から学ぶには判断者への賞賛や非難だけでなく起きた理由を調べる必要がある。

sentences.en: The teacher encourages students to identify which aspects of their preparation they could realistically improve.
sentences.ja: 教師は準備のどの側面を現実的に改善できるか特定するよう促す。

sentences.en: The thought experiment illustrates that uncertainty is an unavoidable feature of many meaningful choices.
sentences.ja: 思考実験は不確実性が多くの意味ある選択に不可避の特徴であることを示す。

sentences.en: A reasonable decision can produce a disappointing result, just as a poorly considered decision can occasionally lead to success.
sentences.ja: 合理的判断が期待外れの結果を生むことも、十分に検討しない判断が時に成功を生むこともある。

sentences.en: A more useful evaluation considers the evidence available at the time together with what later experience has taught the decision maker.
sentences.ja: より有益な評価は当時の根拠と後の経験から学んだことを合わせて考える。

sentences.en: For the students, this approach creates an opportunity to improve their judgment without pretending that they can control every possible outcome.
sentences.ja: 生徒にとってこの方法は全結果を制御できると装わず判断を改善する機会になる。

vocabulary.definition: in a way suited to reality
behaving as though something were true

questions.prompt: Why did students make different choices?
What was unknown at the time?
How did classmates judge the choices?
options: By the students' prior preparation only.
By the favorable or unfavorable outcome.
To test whether outcomes affect judgment of decisions.
To prove the events were identical.
They always prove decisions were good.
They may reveal useful lessons about assumptions.
They must be used only to blame people.
Evaluate decisions using prior evidence and later lessons, not results alone.
Every successful outcome proves wise judgment.
Uncertainty makes all choices equally good.

paraphrases.source: At this point, neither student knows whether the event selected will turn out as expected.
paraphrases.rewrite: Neither student can yet know how the chosen event will proceed.

paraphrases.source: Their teacher asks whether the judgments would have been different if the two outcomes had been reversed through circumstances beyond the students' control.
paraphrases.rewrite: The teacher asks whether swapped outcomes would have changed the class's assessments.

paraphrases.source: The students review the information that had been available before each decision was made, rather than treating later discoveries as though they had been known beforehand.
paraphrases.rewrite: They do not assume information discovered later was available earlier.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 事後情報を事前扱いしない。

paraphrases.source: A reasonable decision can produce a disappointing result, just as a poorly considered decision can occasionally lead to success.
paraphrases.rewrite: Sound choices sometimes end badly, and poorly reasoned choices sometimes succeed.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 判断と結果は一致しない。

cloze.explanation_ja: 不確実性は避けられない。
